I have resolved the issue where deferred fields were incorrect when following prefetches back to the parent object.

### Root Cause
When executing `prefetch_related` queries across forward or reverse relations (`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`, `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`, and `ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`), their `get_prefetch_queryset` methods automatically populated the reverse relation cache on each related object (`rel_obj`) pointing back to the parent `instance`.

Two problems occurred:
1. If the parent `instance` was loaded with deferred fields (e.g. via `.only()` or `.defer()`), the incomplete instance was cached on `rel_obj`, causing subsequent attribute accesses on `rel_obj`'s relation to see deferred fields and trigger unnecessary database queries.
2. Even if `rel_obj` had its own nested `Prefetch` or was already cached (e.g. via `select_related` or custom prefetch queryset), `get_prefetch_queryset` unconditionally overwritten the cached relation on `rel_obj` with the parent `instance`.

### Fix
In [`ForwardManyToOneDescriptor`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L82), [`ReverseOneToOneDescriptor`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L329), and [`ReverseManyToOneDescriptor`](file:///testbed/django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py#L500):
- Exclude parent instances with deferred fields (`not inst.get_deferred_fields()`) from being assigned to the reverse cache on `rel_obj`.
- Check that the reverse relation is not already cached on `rel_obj` before setting the cached value, preventing overwriting of nested prefetches or select_related instances.
